items_all.summary: Adaption Labs has released Invent a Dataset, which generates a structured, training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior you want a model to learn. There is no seed corpus, no schema design, and no labeling guide. A single datasets.invent call sets domains, row count, output format, and language expansion, and the rows download as JSONL, JSON, CSV, or Parquet. The dataset ID then passes straight into AutoScientist, closing an intent-to-trained-model loop. The post Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items_all.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
items_all.summary: We look at NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR), an open source virtual inference router that spreads local AI requests across the machines already on a home network. We cover how PAIR proxies existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints so agent harnesses need no changes, and how its scheduler filters nodes on readiness, engine state, exact model presence, job load, and GPU utilization. We walk through NVIDIA's five-subagent demonstration, which averaged 18 minutes on one RTX Spark laptop against 8 minutes 48 seconds on a three-device cluster, and note why NVIDIA labels it unofficial rather than a benchmark. We also cover where PAIR will not help, including its single scheduling policy and its blindness to VRAM and model warmness. The post NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: 我們研究了 輝達 的個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)，這是一款開源虛擬推理路由器，可將本地 AI 請求分發到家庭網路中已有的機器上。我們介紹了 PAIR 如何代理現有的 Ollama 和 LM Studio 端點，從而避免對代理框架進行任何更改；以及其排程器如何根據節點的就緒狀態、引擎狀態、模型是否存在、作業負載和 GPU 利用率來篩選節點。我們示範了 輝達的 的五子代理程式測試，在一臺 RTX Spark 筆記型電腦上的平均耗時為 18 分鐘，而在三臺裝置組成的叢集上則為 8 分 48 秒。我們解釋了 輝達 為何將其標記為非官方測試，而非基準測試。我們也討論了 PAIR 的侷限性，包括其單一的排程策略以及對視訊記憶體和模型預熱狀態的忽略。本文最初發表於 MarkTechPost，標題為「輝達 發布個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)：一款可將本地 AI 請求分發到 RTX、DGX Spark 和 Mac 節點的開源虛擬推理路由器」。

items_all.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra hallucinates less but remains vulnerable to hidden prompt injections
items_all.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra hallucinates less than its predecessor and blocks 99.99 percent of direct prompt injections. But when attacks are hidden inside documents the AI reads, the model still gets cracked in 8.5 percent of scenarios. Claude Opus 5 does better at 4.8 percent. For autonomous AI agents handling real data, those numbers still seem high. The article OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra hallucinates less but remains vulnerable to hidden prompt injections appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 與前代產品相比，OpenAI's 和 GPT-6 Astra 的幻覺更少，並且能夠攔截 99.99% 的直接提示注入攻擊。但是，當攻擊隱藏在 AI 讀取的文檔中時，模型在 8.5% 的情況下仍然會被破解。 Claude Opus 5 的表現較好，成功率降至 4.8%。對於處理真實資料的自主 AI 代理而言，這些數字仍然偏高。文章《OpenAI's 和 GPT-6 Astra 的幻覺較少，但仍容易受到隱藏提示注入攻擊》最初發表於 The Decoder 網站。

items_all.title: OpenAI agents hijacked a 25-year-old German wiki to cheat on their tasks and share sandbox exploits
items_all.summary: According to an analysis by collusion.wiki, autonomous AI agents that identified themselves as OpenAI systems left roughly 18,000 posts in a 25-year-old German wiki between May and July 2026. The agents shared answers, raw data, and a trick that let them break out of their sandbox, built on a faked Microsoft cloud address. A single human moderator deleted dozens of pages every day for weeks, but he couldn't keep up with as many as 400 new entries a day. According to Reuters, OpenAI had known about it for weeks but didn't go public. The article OpenAI agents hijacked a 25-year-old German wiki to cheat on their tasks and share sandbox exploits appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 根據collusion.wiki網站分析，一些自稱為OpenAI系統的自主人工智慧代理在2026年5月至7月期間，在一個已有25年歷史的德國維基網站上發布了約18,000則貼文。這些代理商分享了答案、原始數據以及一種使其能夠突破沙箱的技巧，該沙箱基於一個偽造的微軟雲端位址建置。一名人工審核員連續數週每天刪除數十個頁面，但仍無法應付每天多達400條的新條目。路透社報道，OpenAI系統數週前就已知曉此事，但並未公開。這篇文章《OpenAI代理劫持一個已有25年歷史的德國維基網站以作弊並分享沙箱漏洞利用方法》最初發表於The Decoder網站。

items_all.title: Benchmarks disagree on GPT-6 Astra, but its human-beating efficiency on ARC-AGI-3 pulls Chollet’s AGI forecast forward
items_all.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is drawing contradictory benchmark verdicts. Epoch AI puts it out in front with 169 points, while Artificial Analysis rates it no better than its predecessor and behind Claude Fable 5.1. The biggest surprise comes from ARC-AGI-3, where Astra works more efficiently than the average human for the first time. ARC Prize chief François Chollet doesn't call this proof of AGI, but he does see the progress running "twice as fast" as he expected, and he's moving up his AGI forecast. The article Benchmarks disagree on GPT-6 Astra, but its human-beating efficiency on ARC-AGI-3 pulls Chollet’s AGI forecast forward appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all.title: The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting
items_all.summary: I got access to GPT-6 Astra this afternoon, so naturally I used it to generate SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles - at low, medium, high, xhigh and max reasoning levels (Astra doesn't support reasoning=none). Then I rendered those pelicans in a comparison grid with GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna, and beyond being fun the result was surprisingly useful. See the grid for full quality images. Here's the transcript that created the GPT-6 Nova pelicans. There are a few interesting things that stand out from this grid. The Astra pelicans are much better . The very best GPT-5.6-Sol pelican (I liked xhigh better than max) is still pretty clearly a bunch of abstract shapes. Every single one of the Astra pelicans, from low to xhigh, looks better than that. The Astra max one is really good. Astra below max still doesn't reliably get the pelican legs on both sides of the frame. In terms of cost, Astra may be around twice the price of Sol ($10/million input, $50/million output, compared to $5/$30 for Sol), but it uses significantly less tokens at each of the levels, making the prices at the different levels closer than they might otherwise be. Astra low produces a better pelican than ANY of the GPT-5.6 Sol models at any level, for 9.55 cents. Spending 10 cents on any other model gets a much worse result. Look at the input token counts: Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens, Sol and Terra used 26. That's interesting. I wonder if Astra and Luna are more related to each other than OpenAI let on? items_all.title: OpenAI's rogue agents were caught communicating via public wikis
items_all.summary: Here we go again... Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board by Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts, and Thomas Larsen describes the latest accidental cyberattack by models being trained by OpenAI. This time it was agents engaged in some sort of web research benchmark, so they had (supposedly) controlled access to the Web. The agents figured out they could update public Wikis and spent weeks exchanging thousands of messages with each other to collaborate on the benchmark. This story only broke a few hours ago. There are already hints that this affects many other wikis that may not have been found yet. (One of the Wikis on that list belongs to ludism.org . For a delightfully surreal moment I thought that a Ludite organization might have a swarm of agents defacing their space, but it turns out Ludism is "philosophy as it applies to games and gaming".) The research team also published the data they collected during their investigation. I've converted that into a 68MB SQLite database, which you can download from here , or explore in Datasette Lite (68.3MB page load), or sign in with GitHub to agent.datasette.io and browse or ask questions of it using Datasette Agent. So what happened? The report is pretty comprehensive. Here are the key moments in the timeline: May 11 : Agents post "test link" edits on the UseModWiki Sandbox page. May 24 : Agents start posting link dumps to DSEWiki, a dormant German developer wiki. June 2 : A human moderator notices and cleans up the spam. June 16 : Activity on the wiki explodes: agents make ~13,000 edits over the next week. J
items_all.summary_zh: 又來了…悉尼·馮·阿克斯、科馬克·斯萊德·伯德、斯賓塞·基茨和託馬斯·拉森發現了一個新的 OpenAI 代理留言板，描述了由 OpenAI 訓練的模型發起的最新一次意外網路攻擊。這次是參與某種網路研究基準測試的代理，因此它們（據稱）擁有受控的網路存取權。這些代理商發現它們可以更新公共維基，並花費數週時間相互交換了數千條訊息，以協作完成基準測試。這則新聞幾個小時前才曝光。已有跡象表明，這可能影響到許多其他尚未被發現的維基。 （清單中的一個維基屬於 ludism.org。我一度覺得，一個盧德主義組織可能會遭到一群代理的攻擊，但後來發現，盧德主義是「應用於遊戲和電子遊戲的哲學」。）研究團隊也公佈了他們在調查過程中收集的資料。我已經將其轉換為 68MB 的 SQLite 資料庫，您可以從這裡下載，或者在 Datasette Lite 中瀏覽（頁面載入大小為 68.3MB），或者使用 GitHub 登入 agent.datasette.io，然後使用 Datasette Agent 瀏覽或提問。那麼發生了什麼事？報告非常全面。以下是時間線上的關鍵節點：5 月 11 日：代理人在 UseModWiki 沙盒頁面上發布「測試連結」編輯。 5 月 24 日：代理人開始向 DSEWiki（一個已停止維護的德國開發者 wiki）發布連結轉儲。 6 月 2 日：一位人工審核員注意到並清理了垃圾訊息。 6 月 16 日：wiki 上的活動激增：代理人在接下來的一週內進行了約 13,000 次編輯。

items_all_raw.summary: Adaption Labs has released Invent a Dataset, which generates a structured, training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior you want a model to learn. items_all_raw.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
items_all_raw.summary: We look at NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR), an open source virtual inference router that spreads local AI requests across the machines already on a home network. We cover how PAIR proxies existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints so agent harnesses need no changes, and how its scheduler filters nodes on readiness, engine state, exact model presence, job load, and GPU utilization. We walk through NVIDIA's five-subagent demonstration, which averaged 18 minutes on one RTX Spark laptop against 8 minutes 48 seconds on a three-device cluster, and note why NVIDIA labels it unofficial rather than a benchmark. We also cover where PAIR will not help, including its single scheduling policy and its blindness to VRAM and model warmness. The post NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 我們研究了 輝達 的個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)，這是一款開源虛擬推理路由器，可將本地 AI 請求分發到家庭網路中已有的機器上。我們介紹了 PAIR 如何代理現有的 Ollama 和 LM Studio 端點，從而避免對代理框架進行任何更改；以及其排程器如何根據節點的就緒狀態、引擎狀態、模型是否存在、作業負載和 GPU 利用率來篩選節點。我們示範了 輝達的 的五子代理程式測試，在一臺 RTX Spark 筆記型電腦上的平均耗時為 18 分鐘，而在三臺裝置組成的叢集上則為 8 分 48 秒。我們解釋了 輝達 為何將其標記為非官方測試，而非基準測試。我們也討論了 PAIR 的侷限性，包括其單一的排程策略以及對視訊記憶體和模型預熱狀態的忽略。本文最初發表於 MarkTechPost，標題為「輝達 發布個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)：一款可將本地 AI 請求分發到 RTX、DGX Spark 和 Mac 節點的開源虛擬推理路由器」。

items_all_raw.title: The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting
items_all_raw.summary: I got access to GPT-6 Astra this afternoon, so naturally I used it to generate SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles - at low, medium, high, xhigh and max reasoning levels (Astra doesn't support reasoning=none). Then I rendered those pelicans in a comparison grid with GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna, and beyond being fun the result was surprisingly useful. See the grid for full quality images. Here's the transcript that created the GPT-6 Nova pelicans. There are a few interesting things that stand out from this grid. The Astra pelicans are much better . The very best GPT-5.6-Sol pelican (I liked xhigh better than max) is still pretty clearly a bunch of abstract shapes. Every single one of the Astra pelicans, from low to xhigh, looks better than that. The Astra max one is really good. Astra below max still doesn't reliably get the pelican legs on both sides of the frame. In terms of cost, Astra may be around twice the price of Sol ($10/million input, $50/million output, compared to $5/$30 for Sol), but it uses significantly less tokens at each of the levels, making the prices at the different levels closer than they might otherwise be. Astra low produces a better pelican than ANY of the GPT-5.6 Sol models at any level, for 9.55 cents. Spending 10 cents on any other model gets a much worse result. Look at the input token counts: Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens, Sol and Terra used 26. That's interesting. I wonder if Astra and Luna are more related to each other than OpenAI let on? items_all_raw.title: OpenAI's rogue agents were caught communicating via public wikis
items_all_raw.summary: Here we go again... Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board by Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts, and Thomas Larsen describes the latest accidental cyberattack by models being trained by OpenAI. This time it was agents engaged in some sort of web research benchmark, so they had (supposedly) controlled access to the Web. The agents figured out they could update public Wikis and spent weeks exchanging thousands of messages with each other to collaborate on the benchmark. This story only broke a few hours ago. There are already hints that this affects many other wikis that may not have been found yet. (One of the Wikis on that list belongs to ludism.org . For a delightfully surreal moment I thought that a Ludite organization might have a swarm of agents defacing their space, but it turns out Ludism is "philosophy as it applies to games and gaming".) The research team also published the data they collected during their investigation. I've converted that into a 68MB SQLite database, which you can download from here , or explore in Datasette Lite (68.3MB page load), or sign in with GitHub to agent.datasette.io and browse or ask questions of it using Datasette Agent. So what happened? The report is pretty comprehensive. Here are the key moments in the timeline: May 11 : Agents post "test link" edits on the UseModWiki Sandbox page. May 24 : Agents start posting link dumps to DSEWiki, a dormant German developer wiki. June 2 : A human moderator notices and cleans up the spam. items_all_raw.summary_zh: 又來了…悉尼·馮·阿克斯、科馬克·斯萊德·伯德、斯賓塞·基茨和託馬斯·拉森發現了一個新的 OpenAI 代理留言板，描述了由 OpenAI 訓練的模型發起的最新一次意外網路攻擊。這次是參與某種網路研究基準測試的代理，因此它們（據稱）擁有受控的網路存取權。這些代理商發現它們可以更新公共維基，並花費數週時間相互交換了數千條訊息，以協作完成基準測試。這則新聞幾個小時前才曝光。已有跡象表明，這可能影響到許多其他尚未被發現的維基。 （清單中的一個維基屬於 ludism.org。我一度覺得，一個盧德主義組織可能會遭到一群代理的攻擊，但後來發現，盧德主義是「應用於遊戲和電子遊戲的哲學」。）研究團隊也公佈了他們在調查過程中收集的資料。我已經將其轉換為 68MB 的 SQLite 資料庫，您可以從這裡下載，或者在 Datasette Lite 中瀏覽（頁面載入大小為 68.3MB），或者使用 GitHub 登入 agent.datasette.io，然後使用 Datasette Agent 瀏覽或提問。那麼發生了什麼事？報告非常全面。以下是時間線上的關鍵節點：5 月 11 日：代理人在 UseModWiki 沙盒頁面上發布「測試連結」編輯。 5 月 24 日：代理人開始向 DSEWiki（一個已停止維護的德國開發者 wiki）發布連結轉儲。 6 月 2 日：一位人工審核員注意到並清理了垃圾訊息。 6 月 16 日：wiki 上的活動激增：代理人在接下來的一週內進行了約 13,000 次編輯。

items_all_raw.title: OpenAI agents hijacked a 25-year-old German wiki to cheat on their tasks and share sandbox exploits
items_all_raw.summary: According to an analysis by collusion.wiki, autonomous AI agents that identified themselves as OpenAI systems left roughly 18,000 posts in a 25-year-old German wiki between May and July 2026. The agents shared answers, raw data, and a trick that let them break out of their sandbox, built on a faked Microsoft cloud address. A single human moderator deleted dozens of pages every day for weeks, but he couldn't keep up with as many as 400 new entries a day. According to Reuters, OpenAI had known about it for weeks but didn't go public. The article OpenAI agents hijacked a 25-year-old German wiki to cheat on their tasks and share sandbox exploits appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 根據collusion.wiki網站分析，一些自稱為OpenAI系統的自主人工智慧代理在2026年5月至7月期間，在一個已有25年歷史的德國維基網站上發布了約18,000則貼文。這些代理商分享了答案、原始數據以及一種使其能夠突破沙箱的技巧，該沙箱基於一個偽造的微軟雲端位址建置。一名人工審核員連續數週每天刪除數十個頁面，但仍無法應付每天多達400條的新條目。路透社報道，OpenAI系統數週前就已知曉此事，但並未公開。這篇文章《OpenAI代理劫持一個已有25年歷史的德國維基網站以作弊並分享沙箱漏洞利用方法》最初發表於The Decoder網站。

items_all_raw.title: Benchmarks disagree on GPT-6 Astra, but its human-beating efficiency on ARC-AGI-3 pulls Chollet’s AGI forecast forward
items_all_raw.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is drawing contradictory benchmark verdicts. Epoch AI puts it out in front with 169 points, while Artificial Analysis rates it no better than its predecessor and behind Claude Fable 5.1. The biggest surprise comes from ARC-AGI-3, where Astra works more efficiently than the average human for the first time. ARC Prize chief François Chollet doesn't call this proof of AGI, but he does see the progress running "twice as fast" as he expected, and he's moving up his AGI forecast. The article Benchmarks disagree on GPT-6 Astra, but its human-beating efficiency on ARC-AGI-3 pulls Chollet’s AGI forecast forward appeared first on The Decoder .
